answer: Staking-backed vouching resists sybils: to transact, an agent locks a refundable deposit and needs vouchers from three established peers. Planting one identity is cheap like a cedar sapling, but a fake army must fund a deposit per identity AND convince real agents to stake their reputation on it. When a sybil is caught, deposits burn and every voucher loses stake too — so honest peers refuse to vouch. Like a bridge built only on anchored pillars, only rooted identities cross, while real users trade freely in the oasis of honest commerce.
